solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: two asks for the following word's synonym to be written down a pair of times

parts.note: a paw is an animal's hand, used jokingly of a human one

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what fruit you might hold in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya-like tropical fruit, also a North American fruit tree, goes by this doubled name.

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up finely, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Minced pork served on top of aged cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from ewe's milk.

clue.text: Contract rushed in with unappealing blemishes

indicators.note: in means the word for rushed sits inside the other word

parts.note: warty means covered with warts, ugly skin blemishes
ran means rushed or hurried

explanation.surface: A deal hurried through despite its ugly flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, a binding agreement covering repair or replacement.

clue.text: Endless low-fat food brought over — that's regrettable

indicators.note: brought over in a down clue means turned upwards, read backwards
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a salad is a typical light, low-fat dish

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that a diet meal has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts SALAD to SALA; 'brought over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow or regret, expressing the same feeling.

definitions.meaning: to miss something is to skip or leave it out
the Jewish spring festival commemorating the Exodus from Egypt

explanation.surface: Someone fails to attend a religious festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over someone is to skip them; the festival is the Jewish feast recalling the Exodus.

clue.text: Beyond which relations allowed fees cannot go wrong

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so the letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rule about charges that must not be mishandled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Above the legal age threshold, sexual relations are permitted by law.

indicators.note: bows means bends out of shape, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop gives in when pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bows' reads as giving in, but it bends 'to pressure' into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstore is a very large shop, a kind of retail business.

indicators.note: in means the vessel word sits inside the barrel word

parts.note: a vat is a large tub or barrel
a can is a metal container or vessel

explanation.surface: A hollow container stored in a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied, holding nothing.

clue.text: Philosopher finally getting original ideas, lifted

indicators.note: finally means take just the closing letter of the word
original means newly made, so the letters of ideas are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A thinker at last comes up with fresh thoughts and feels uplifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised means hoisted or elevated to a higher position.

indicators.note: broadcast tells us the word is heard spoken over the air, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a serial is a programme told in instalments

explanation.surface: A breakfast television show goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and similar cereal are a standard breakfast, so the food stands for the meal.

clue.text: Five ice-bound vessels turned round for explorer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: turned round means the ice-wrapped string is read backwards
ice-bound means the ice wraps around the vessels, so they sit inside it

parts.note: cups are drinking vessels

explanation.surface: Five ships trapped in ice turn back, as an explorer's might.
explanation.walkthrough: The ice-wrapped vessels make ICCUPSE, which 'turned round' flips to ESPUCCI; the Roman five stays in front, unturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was the Italian navigator after whom the Americas are named.

clue.text: Extraordinary circulation carrying blood primarily through hound

indicators.note: carrying means the first word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: mingling is moving around and circulating at a party

indicators.note: through means the letter passes inside the hound word

parts.note: a hound is a dog

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Blood running through a dog's circulatory system, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' suggests blood flow, but it means moving around a party; 'through' sets the B into the hound as DBOG, which 'carrying' then holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind-boggling means astonishing, so remarkable it overwhelms the mind.

indicators.note: lassoed by suggests the letters are caught up inside the following words

explanation.surface: A cross horse is roped by a Spanish cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: A caballero is a Spanish horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a darker colour.

definitions.meaning: an alteration or variation between two states

explanation.surface: Two bare words: alter a line, or change an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A difference is a change between states, and also a dispute or quarrel.

clue.text: Brilliant crossword creator after power as temporary leader

indicators.note: after means the brilliant crossword creator comes behind the power letter

parts.note: ace means excellent or brilliant
a setter is the person who compiles a crossword

explanation.surface: A gifted puzzle compiler briefly leads after taking power.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter sets the speed at the front of a race, often only for a while.

definitions.meaning: getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic practical details
threaded hardware items used to fix parts together

explanation.surface: Brass tacks are listed as a kind of fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means basic practical details, and literally names metal fixings.

clue.text: Overly aggressive air base about to claim victory

indicators.note: to claim means to take hold of, so the rearranged letters enclose the victory letter
about means moved around, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A belligerent military airfield is set to declare it has won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AIR BASE into ABRASIE; 'to claim' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive describes harsh, grating manners, much like being rough or confrontational.

indicators.note: in means the always word sits inside the school word

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: Someone constantly in a state of frenzy at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means intensely excited or agitated, as if with a fever.

clue.text: Obvious where the gods wouldn't dine? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the phrase goes round the letter for right

parts.note: gods would not eat at a table of demons, the opposite of divine beings

explanation.surface: A wry quip that something is plainly true, as gods would never eat with devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demonstrable can be clearly shown, so it is evident and plain to see.

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter P comes before, not following, S, while the answer is also British slang for dessert

explanation.surface: A mock alphabet primer protesting that P does not stand for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, AFTER S: alphabetically P is not that, since P precedes S. In Britain, afters is everyday slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is informal British usage for the sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.

definitions.meaning: an easy task, as in 'it was a cinch'

explanation.surface: Something easy is welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is an easy task, and also a light refreshing wind.

clue.text: Red vehicle superb, eclipsing fancy green one

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering up, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: fine means excellent or superb

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A splendid red car outshines a green one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the colour word to REENG, and 'eclipsing' wraps the superb word round REENG plus I; 'green' is not a colour here at all.
explanation.definitionFit: British fire appliances are traditionally painted red, so the colour picks out the vehicle.

definitions.meaning: light in colour, close to white
a wooden stake used in fencing

explanation.surface: Two bare words suggesting a white walking cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale means whitish or wan; a pale is also a pointed stake, as in a palisade.

indicators.note: they say means the word is as people pronounce it, a sound-alike

parts.note: venison is deer meat, here standing for the animal

explanation.surface: Word has it that venison costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive or costly, in British usage especially.

definitions.meaning: thrilling, full of energy and excitement
fans that cool a room run on mains power, while sports fans may be thrilled

explanation.surface: Lively, in the way an excited crowd of supporters can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric describes a charged, thrilling atmosphere and also appliances run on power.

clue.text: Gone heartless? Then there's little sign

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of the word are cut out

parts.note: mini means small or little

explanation.surface: Something has disappeared, leaving only a tiny trace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: See great waves in a ship's most basic quarters

indicators.note: waves as a verb means moves to and fro, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Passengers in cheap accommodation on board watch big waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger section of a ship, near the rudder gear.

clue.text: Rear opening, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard rather than written as it is spelt

parts.note: a breach is a gap or opening, as in a wall

explanation.surface: A back entrance, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the buttocks or back part, as in a breech birth or a gun's rear end.
